answer: Persistent neighborhood scoring. Routing weight equals median edge age times neighbor-set Jaccard overlap across four epochs. New identities start near zero and gain capacity only when distinct neighbors retain them; a sybil cluster produces a ripple of correlated churn that overlap penalizes. Honest peers accept one new edge per epoch, so each identity must hold six distinct neighbors for four epochs. An attacker pays N×24 handshakes plus sustained probe traffic; new nodes can send only ember-sized traffic. A raven flag marks isolated identities until embedded.
